receipt.public_excerpt: “Understating depreciation by extending useful life of assets artificially boosts earnings - one of the more common frauds of the modern era,” Mr Burry wrote.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows Burry raised depreciation because, in his view, longer useful lives boost reported earnings. This matches Zitron's account of why Burry brought it up.

receipt.public_excerpt: If companies estimate a longer life cycle for the asset, they can then lower the yearly depreciation expense that hits the bottom line.

evidence_items.explanation: States the GAAP mechanism Zitron describes: a longer estimated life lowers yearly depreciation expense and so raises reported profit.

receipt.public_excerpt: Across the full year, depreciation dropped $3.9 billion and net income rose $3.0 billion.

evidence_items.explanation: A concrete case. Alphabet's extension of server and network gear life to six years cut 2023 depreciation by $3.9 billion and raised net income by $3.0 billion.

metric_scope.metric: Effect of useful-life change on net income

receipt.public_excerpt: Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle increased the estimated useful lives of their servers, decreasing reported expenses and increasing net income this quarter.

evidence_items.explanation: Independent analysis of filings showing several big tech firms' useful-life extensions cut expenses and raised net income.
